# Global Init & Harness Removal

**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Status:** Approved

## Summary

Rework the `pup init` / `pup install` / `pup add` / `pup update` command model to mirror pi.dev's philosophy: global initialization by default, with opt-in local project configuration. Remove the `harness` property from `config.json` in favor of auto-detecting all available agent harnesses at runtime.

## Motivation

Currently, `pup init` creates a local `.powerups/` folder and requires you to be inside a project that has one to run most commands (`validate`, `info`, `use`). This breaks the workflow where powerups are initialized globally and used from any directory. The stored `harness` property in `config.json` is also unnecessary — harnesses can be auto-detected from the agent folders present on the machine.

## Command Structure

### `pup init` (changed — global only)

- Creates `~/.powerups/` + global `config.json` (`{ packages: [] }`)
- Auto-detects all agent harnesses present on the machine (`~/.claude`, `~/.pi/agent`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.codex`)
- Scaffolds docs (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md + skill files) to **all** detected harness locations in the home directory
- If no harness is detected, requires `--harness <name>` to proceed
- Throws if `~/.powerups/` already exists

### `pup project init` (new subcommand)

- `project` is a new command group with `init` as its first subcommand
- Creates `.powerups/` + `config.json` (`{ packages: [] }`) in the current project root
- No harness scaffolding — purely creates the local config gate
- Throws if `.powerups/` already exists

### `pup install <source>` (changed — default flipped)

- Installs to **global** store (`~/.powerups/`) by default
- `-l` / `--local` flag installs to the local `.powerups/` store instead
- `-l` requires `pup project init` to have been run (local folder must exist)
- Global install requires `pup init` to have been run (global folder must exist)
- Removes the `-g` / `--global` flag (it is now the default)

### `pup add <source>` (changed — requires project init)

- Same behavior as now (adds package to local config), but errors explicitly if `.powerups/config.json` doesn't exist instead of silently no-oping
- Error message guides the user to run `pup project init` first

### `pup update` (changed — global only, multi-harness)

- Always targets `~/` (global), regardless of where it is run
- Auto-detects all harness folders and re-scaffolds docs to all of them
- `--harness` flag only used when detection finds nothing (explicit override)
- No longer reads `harness` from config (it is removed)

### `pup use <name>` (unchanged behavior, clarified error)

- Still requires local `.powerups/config.json` (project init)
- Error message updated to guide user to run `pup project init` if missing

### `pup validate <name>` (changed — works anywhere)

- Removes the hard error when `.powerups` doesn't exist
- Uses merged resolution: local config packages first, then global config packages as fallback
- Works from any directory

### `pup info <name>` (changed — works anywhere)

- Same as validate — removes `.powerups` requirement, uses merged resolution

### `pup list` (minor update)

- Already scans both local + global stores and handles null config gracefully
- Add global config's registered sources to the `registeredSources` filter set (currently only reads local config)

## Command Tiers

**Project-gated** (require `pup project init` first):
- `pup use` — needs local config for per-project metrics tracking
- `pup add` — needs local config to register packages for that project
- `pup install -l` — needs local `.powerups/` store to exist

**Work anywhere** (fall back to global config when no local `.powerups`):
- `pup list` — scans both stores
- `pup validate` — merged resolution (local + global, local priority)
- `pup info` — merged resolution (local + global, local priority)

**Global-gated** (require `pup init` first):
- `pup update` — re-scaffolds global docs
- `pup install` (default/global) — needs global store to exist

## Config & Harness Removal

### `config.json` changes

- Remove `harness` from `Config` type entirely → `{ packages: PackageEntry[] }`
- Both project and global config use the same shape and same schema
- `writeConfig` / `writeGlobalConfig` never write `harness`
- Clean break — old configs with `harness` will fail validation on read

### `detectHarness` → `detectHarnesses`

- Returns `Harness[]` instead of `Harness`
- Global fingerprints only: `~/.claude`, `~/.pi/agent`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.codex`
- `--harness` flag → validate and return `[single harness]`
- Multiple detected → return all (no error)
- None detected, no flag → throw `no_harness_detected`
- Remove `skipGlobal` option and local fingerprint scanning

### `scaffold` changes

- Accepts `Harness[]`, loops over all harnesses, writes instruction + skill files to each
- `ScaffoldResult` → `{ harnesses: Harness[], filesWritten: string[] }`
- Always operates on the home directory (global)

### `update` command changes

- Calls `detectHarnesses(homeDir, harnessFlag)` → array → `scaffold`
- No config read/write for harness
- `--harness` flag only for "nothing detected" case
- No longer persists anything to config after scaffolding

## Powerup Resolution Model

### `resolvePowerUp` (for `use` — local only, gatekept)

- Reads local config only (`.powerups/config.json`)
- If no local config exists → throw error guiding user to run `pup project init`
- Searches only packages registered in local config
- Local store packages prioritized over global store on name collision (unchanged)

### `resolvePowerUp` with `fallbackToGlobal: true` (for `validate` / `info` — merged)

- Reads local config (if exists) **and** global config, merges their package lists
- Local config packages take priority on name collisions
- If neither local nor global config exists → throw `powerups is not initialized — run 'pup init' first`
- Search order: for each package in the merged list, resolve its location (local store first, then global store)

### Implementation

Add a `fallbackToGlobal` boolean parameter to `resolvePowerUp` rather than creating a separate function. When `true`, it merges global config packages into the search set. When `false` (the `use` case), it behaves as today but with a better error.

## Error Handling

### New / changed errors

| Command | Condition | Error message |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | `~/.powerups/` already exists | `powerups is already initialized globally` |
| `project init` | `.powerups/` already exists | `powerups is already initialized for this project` |
| `add` | No `.powerups/config.json` | `powerups is not initialized for this project — run 'pup project init' first` |
| `use` | No `.powerups/config.json` | Same as above |
| `install -l` | No `.powerups/` folder | Same as above |
| `install` (global) | No `~/.powerups/` folder | `powerups is not initialized — run 'pup init' first` |
| `validate` / `info` | Neither local nor global config exists | `powerups is not initialized — run 'pup init' first` |
| `update` | No `~/.powerups/` folder | `powerups is not initialized — run 'pup init' first` |
| `update` | No harnesses detected, no `--harness` flag | `no harness detected — pass --harness to specify one` |

### Errors to remove

- `multiple_harnesses_detected` — no longer an error; multiple harnesses are supported
- `update_errors.no_harness_config` — `update` no longer reads harness from config
- `init_errors.dry_folder_exists` — replaced with global-specific message

### Errors to update

- `main_folder_not_found` errors across commands → split into context-appropriate messages (project-level vs global-level)

## File-by-File Changes

### New files

- `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts` — re-export from private (follows `pack.ts` pattern)
- `packages/cli/src/private/commands/project/index.ts` — `project` command group with `init` subcommand
- `packages/cli/src/private/commands/project/init/index.ts` — implementation: creates local `.powerups/` + `config.json` (`{ packages: [] }`), throws if exists
- `packages/cli/src/private/commands/project/init/init.spec.ts` — tests
- `packages/cli/src/private/errors/projectErrors.ts` — project-level errors

### Modified files

| File | Changes |
|---|---|
| `private/commands/init/index.ts` | Target `~/` (global). Detect all harnesses. Scaffold to all. Write global config (no harness). Remove local folder creation. |
| `private/commands/install/index.ts` | Flip default to global. Replace `-g`/`--global` with `-l`/`--local`. Add guard: global needs `~/.powerups/`, local needs `.powerups/`. |
| `private/commands/add/index.ts` | Replace silent no-op with explicit error when no local config. |
| `private/commands/update/index.ts` | Always target `~/`. Call `detectHarnesses`. No config read/write for harness. Guard on global folder. |
| `private/commands/use/index.ts` | Update error message when no local config (guide to `project init`). |

# Global Init & Harness Removal

**Date:** 2026-07-23
**Status:** Approved

## Summary

Rework the `pup init` / `pup install` / `pup add` / `pup update` command model to mirror pi.dev's philosophy: global initialization by default, with opt-in local project configuration. Remove the `harness` property from `config.json` in favor of auto-detecting all available agent harnesses at runtime.

## Motivation

Currently, `pup init` creates a local `.powerups/` folder and requires you to be inside a project that has one to run most commands (`validate`, `info`, `use`). This breaks the workflow where powerups are initialized globally and used from any directory. The stored `harness` property in `config.json` is also unnecessary — harnesses can be auto-detected from the agent folders present on the machine.

## Command Structure

### `pup init` (changed — global only)

- Creates `~/.powerups/` + global `config.json` (`{ packages: [] }`)
- Auto-detects all agent harnesses present on the machine (`~/.claude`, `~/.pi/agent`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.codex`)
- Scaffolds docs (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md + skill files) to **all** detected harness locations in the home directory
- If no harness is detected, requires `--harness <name>` to proceed
- Throws if `~/.powerups/` already exists

### `pup project init` (new subcommand)

- `project` is a new command group with `init` as its first subcommand
- Creates `.powerups/` + `config.json` (`{ packages: [] }`) in the current project root
- No harness scaffolding — purely creates the local config gate
- Throws if `.powerups/` already exists

### `pup install <source>` (changed — default flipped)

- Installs to **global** store (`~/.powerups/`) by default
- `-l` / `--local` flag installs to the local `.powerups/` store instead
- `-l` requires `pup project init` to have been run (local folder must exist)
- Global install requires `pup init` to have been run (global folder must exist)
- Removes the `-g` / `--global` flag (it is now the default)

### `pup add <source>` (changed — requires project init)

- Same behavior as now (adds package to local config), but errors explicitly if `.powerups/config.json` doesn't exist instead of silently no-oping
- Error message guides the user to run `pup project init` first

### `pup update` (changed — global only, multi-harness)

- Always targets `~/` (global), regardless of where it is run
- Auto-detects all harness folders and re-scaffolds docs to all of them
- `--harness` flag only used when detection finds nothing (explicit override)
- No longer reads `harness` from config (it is removed)

### `pup use <name>` (unchanged behavior, clarified error)

- Still requires local `.powerups/config.json` (project init)
- Error message updated to guide user to run `pup project init` if missing

### `pup validate <name>` (changed — works anywhere)

- Removes the hard error when `.powerups` doesn't exist
- Uses merged resolution: local config packages first, then global config packages as fallback
- Works from any directory

### `pup info <name>` (changed — works anywhere)

- Same as validate — removes `.powerups` requirement, uses merged resolution

### `pup list` (minor update)

- Already scans both local + global stores and handles null config gracefully
- Add global config's registered sources to the `registeredSources` filter set (currently only reads local config)

## Command Tiers

**Project-gated** (require `pup project init` first):
- `pup use` — needs local config for per-project metrics tracking
- `pup add` — needs local config to register packages for that project
- `pup install -l` — needs local `.powerups/` store to exist

**Work anywhere** (fall back to global config when no local `.powerups`):
- `pup list` — scans both stores
- `pup validate` — merged resolution (local + global, local priority)
- `pup info` — merged resolution (local + global, local priority)

**Global-gated** (require `pup init` first):
- `pup update` — re-scaffolds global docs
- `pup install` (default/global) — needs global store to exist

## Config & Harness Removal

### `config.json` changes

- Remove `harness` from `Config` type entirely → `{ packages: PackageEntry[] }`
- Both project and global config use the same shape and same schema
- `writeConfig` / `writeGlobalConfig` never write `harness`
- Clean break — old configs with `harness` will fail validation on read

### `detectHarness` → `detectHarnesses`

- Returns `Harness[]` instead of `Harness`
- Global fingerprints only: `~/.claude`, `~/.pi/agent`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.codex`
- `--harness` flag → validate and return `[single harness]`
- Multiple detected → return all (no error)
- None detected, no flag → throw `no_harness_detected`
- Remove `skipGlobal` option and local fingerprint scanning

### `scaffold` changes

- Accepts `Harness[]`, loops over all harnesses, writes instruction + skill files to each
- `ScaffoldResult` → `{ harnesses: Harness[], filesWritten: string[] }`
- Always operates on the home directory (global)

### `update` command changes

- Calls `detectHarnesses(homeDir, harnessFlag)` → array → `scaffold`
- No config read/write for harness
- `--harness` flag only for "nothing detected" case
- No longer persists anything to config after scaffolding

## Powerup Resolution Model

### `resolvePowerUp` (for `use` — local only, gatekept)

- Reads local config only (`.powerups/config.json`)
- If no local config exists → throw error guiding user to run `pup project init`
- Searches only packages registered in local config
- Local store packages prioritized over global store on name collision (unchanged)

### `resolvePowerUp` with `fallbackToGlobal: true` (for `validate` / `info` — merged)

- Reads local config (if exists) **and** global config, merges their package lists
- Local config packages take priority on name collisions
- If neither local nor global config exists → throw `powerups is not initialized — run 'pup init' first`
- Search order: for each package in the merged list, resolve its location (local store first, then global store)

### Implementation

Add a `fallbackToGlobal` boolean parameter to `resolvePowerUp` rather than creating a separate function. When `true`, it merges global config packages into the search set. When `false` (the `use` case), it behaves as today but with a better error.

## Error Handling

### New / changed errors

| Command | Condition | Error message |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | `~/.powerups/` already exists | `powerups is already initialized globally` |
| `project init` | `.powerups/` already exists | `powerups is already initialized for this project` |
| `add` | No `.powerups/config.json` | `powerups is not initialized for this project — run 'pup project init' first` |
| `use` | No `.powerups/config.json` | Same as above |
| `install -l` | No `.powerups/` folder | Same as above |
| `install` (global) | No `~/.powerups/` folder | `powerups is not initialized — run 'pup init' first` |
| `validate` / `info` | Neither local nor global config exists | `powerups is not initialized — run 'pup init' first` |
| `update` | No `~/.powerups/` folder | `powerups is not initialized — run 'pup init' first` |
| `update` | No harnesses detected, no `--harness` flag | `no harness detected — pass --harness to specify one` |

- `multiple_harnesses_detected` — no longer an error; multiple harnesses are supported
- `update_errors.no_harness_config` — `update` no longer reads harness from config
